clue.text: Unethical perfume brought back by a pupil

indicators.note: brought back tells us the word for the scent is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a perfume is a pleasant smell, an aroma
L is the learner plate sign, so a pupil is L

explanation.surface: A student returns with a scent that is somehow morally dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without moral standards is unethical; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Love sickness

definitions.meaning: an old medical sense: a disease or disorder of the body

explanation.definitionFit: The word means fondness, and in older medical use a bodily disease or complaint.

clue.text: Formerly revered figure finds church key cutting a burden

indicators.note: cutting means the church and key letters slice into the burden word

parts.note: an onus is a burden
CE is the Church of England
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A churchman finds that a key slices through a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: OCEANUS was the Titan of the world-encircling river in Greek myth, worshipped in ancient times, hence 'formerly revered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanus was a Titan deity of Greek myth, worshipped in antiquity but no longer.

clue.text: Designing fellows putting forward constructive ideas

definitions.text: Designing fellows putting forward constructive ideas

parts.words: Designing fellows putting forward constructive ideas
parts.note: designing suggests scheming and constructive suggests helpful, but the people design buildings and their ideas are about construction

explanation.definitionFit: Building designers propose plans for construction.

clue.text: Only men go in at such a meeting

indicators.note: go in tells us the two words before it are placed inside the little word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
but can mean only, as in 'but a child'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gathering restricted to males, a stag affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go in at' puts BUTMEN inside AT. The 'meeting' is the point where one structure meets or touches another.
explanation.definitionFit: An abutment is the place where two things join or touch, such as a bridge resting on its support.

clue.text: "I see, not feel, how — they are!" (Coleridge)

definitions.text: "I see, not feel, how — they are!" (Coleridge)

parts.words: "I see, not feel, how — they are!" (Coleridge)
parts.note: a gap to fill from a line in Coleridge's poem Dejection: An Ode, about the stars and the sky

explanation.walkthrough: The line from Coleridge's Dejection: An Ode reads 'I see, not feel, how beautiful they are!', spoken of the sky and stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the quotation describes the stars as lovely.

clue.text: Have an inclination to be a nurse

definitions.meaning: to be likely or inclined to do something
to look after or care for someone

explanation.surface: Someone wants to train in nursing.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both being disposed toward something and caring for the sick.

clue.text: Medal or order showing noble title

indicators.note: order suggests a decoration but tells us to put the letters of medal and or in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A decoration or honour that reveals aristocratic rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank or lands of a count in Britain is a hereditary noble title.

clue.text: Mother of Achilles is not a Greek character

indicators.note: not means the little word is beside it is left out of the name before

parts.note: Thetis, a sea nymph, was the mother of Achilles in Greek myth
taken as written

explanation.surface: Achilles' mother is no Greek person, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not' removes IS from THETIS, leaving THET, and the A follows. 'character' means a letter of the alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Live on a range

parts.note: to live or exist: we are

explanation.surface: Dwelling on an open stretch of grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is an extent or scope, the same as a field or region covered.

clue.text: No wool-gathering stripper!

parts.note: a person who strips sheep of their wool is not merely gathering it; also one who cheats people out of money

explanation.definitionFit: A shearer strips off a fleece, and figuratively one who swindles people strips them of their cash.

clue.text: Place article in plane maybe

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
taken as written
the plane is a kind of tree, so 'maybe' marks an example

explanation.surface: Putting a piece of writing inside an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the plane tree. AINTREE is a racecourse near Liverpool, home of the Grand National horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a racecourse town near Liverpool, so it is a named location.

clue.text: An intimate friend once — and fit to be so

indicators.note: the letters of the three words before are rearranged in order to become a word for that friend

explanation.surface: Someone close long ago, and suitable for the role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be so' asks for the letters of ONCE, AND and FIT to be rearranged so that they become the intimate friend. The dash makes 'once' look like a time adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidante is a woman to whom secrets are entrusted, a close friend.

clue.text: Fancy a fish to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with puts the fish at the start, ahead of the single letter

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: Someone wants a fish as a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or thought that comes to mind, the same as a notion.

clue.text: Offering growth potential, this is highly regarded in the city

definitions.text: Offering growth potential, this is highly regarded in the city

parts.words: Offering growth potential, this is highly regarded in the city
parts.note: sounds like a promising investment in the financial district, but means plants growing on top of a building, high up in town

explanation.definitionFit: A planted area on top of a building lets things grow high above the street.

clue.text: Sainted eccentric taken as a replacement

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd holy person is brought in as a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one thing in place of another means doing it as a substitute.

clue.text: Force in action — very sad

indicators.note: in means the force word sits inside the action word

parts.note: a deed is an action
to press is to force

explanation.surface: Coercion at work leaves someone deeply unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being low in spirits is a synonym of being very unhappy.

clue.text: Obviously not a manual worker

parts.note: manual means done by hand, so a worker named after the other limb, the one at the end of the leg, is not manual

explanation.definitionFit: A liveried servant is named after a body part that is not the hand, which is the joke.

clue.text: Try to reach agreement, but get into a muddle over one point

indicators.note: muddle means the letters of get, into and a are jumbled

parts.note: E is east, one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Bargaining that becomes confused over a single detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddle' rearranges GETINTOA into NEGOTIAT; 'over' is a link, and E for East ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to try to settle terms with someone.

clue.text: Never start on road work without interruption

indicators.note: start of the word Never means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: taken as written
ST is short for street, a road
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Advice never to begin roadworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without a break is continuous, going on without a pause.

clue.text: Denied the necessity to carry a gun

indicators.note: to carry means the necessity word holds the gun word inside it

parts.note: a need is a necessity
gat is old slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Someone refused the requirement to bear arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny something is to cancel or nullify it, to make it void.

clue.text: Heather holds one foot when getting up

indicators.note: holds means the plant word wraps around the letters for one and foot

parts.note: ling is another name for heather
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather balances on one foot as she rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant, called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising or rising up is a synonym of hoisting or getting up.

clue.text: To repeat: some men will claim it at every opportunity

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: People who say they will copy you at every chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'claIM IT AT Every'. The surface hints at copycats, which is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone is to repeat what they do.

clue.text: Stuffing for the discerning?

parts.note: a herb used in stuffing with onion, which is also a word for a wise and discerning person

explanation.definitionFit: The herb goes into stuffing, and the same word means wise, fitting the discerning.

clue.text: The broadcaster's a real pig with little hesitation

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A radio presenter is a nasty person who rarely pauses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcaster' suggests radio or TV, but it is someone who scatters seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: One who scatters seed broadcasts it, so a seed-scatterer is a broadcaster.

clue.text: The non-union man

parts.note: looks like a worker outside a trade union, but means one who wants a region to break away from a political union

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wants independence from a larger state is against the union.

clue.text: Before noon and after is the same in the centre

indicators.note: after places the same word behind the morning abbreviation

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means before noon
id. is short for idem, Latin for the same

explanation.surface: A riddle claiming morning and afternoon are identical at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed among or in the middle of things is surrounded by them.

clue.text: Pure water

definitions.meaning: nothing more than, sheer or utter

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sheer or nothing but, and also a lake.

clue.text: It's news, free, for the viewer

indicators.note: free means let loose, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper advertises that its news costs nothing to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sees an event is an onlooker, someone who views it.

clue.text: A goddess follows in state

indicators.note: follows puts the goddess after the little word in

parts.note: taken as written
Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt

explanation.surface: A goddess comes after, in some official pronouncement.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Leftist leaders painted by Titian?

parts.note: a red is a communist, a leftist
heads are leaders

explanation.surface: Left-wing bosses posing for a Renaissance portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian red is a hair colour named after the Venetian painter, who favoured auburn-haired models.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter Titian is famed for women with reddish hair, so ginger-haired people are his subjects.

clue.text: An explosion due to the cold

definitions.text: An explosion due to the cold

parts.words: An explosion due to the cold
parts.note: suggests a burst pipe in frost, but means a sudden blast through the nose caused by a head cold

explanation.definitionFit: A head cold causes sudden violent bursts of air from the nose.
